added_claim_errors: The minimum formula is wrong: with $4,000 compensation and $2,000 already contributed, it permits $4,000 rather than $2,000.
"Your 2004 account passes the 15-year test" assumes uninterrupted beneficiary history without establishing it.
"If the money lands in January ... the 2026 room is lost" is wrong: designation for 2026 is federally possible through April 15, 2027, subject to plan processing.
"If annual limits rise, it could take fewer years" is unsupported by announced limits; even four years at $8,000 totals only $32,000.
"The 529 plan probably will not verify his income or other contributions" is an unsupported prediction about an unidentified plan.
"Subtract that too" after taking the minimum can understate eligibility: with $3,000 eligible funds, ample compensation and $2,000 other IRA contributions, it gives $1,000 instead of $3,000.

"Scholarships ... do not" count is too categorical: certain taxable scholarships and graduate stipends qualify, as confirmed in the opened [IRS Publication 590-A](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p590a).
"He is 22" is not established: someone born in 2004 could still be 21 on the request date.
"The transfer must be completed by December 31, 2026" is wrong: the federal deadline for a 2026-designated rollover is April 15, 2027, subject to plan processing.
"Form 1099-Q to you as account owner" is wrong for this direct rollover: the beneficiary is the recipient under the opened [IRS Form 1099-Q instructions](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1099q.pdf).

reasons: B wins narrowly: it includes the income-limit exception and beneficiary-history check, while A's formula can authorize an excess contribution; B's subtraction-order error instead understates eligibility in some cases. Both immediately reject the $48,000 premise, but both give the wrong federal deadline and omit the $40,500 excess calculation and Roth-side 6% excise/correction rules. B adds incorrect scholarship and tax-form advice, while A is more repetitive and speculates about completing the lifetime rollover sooner. I opened the linked [GovInfo bill](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s5550is/html/BILLS-119s5550is.htm) and [historical state summary](https://praetorianguard.biz/resources/slott-reports/state-tax-treatment-of-529-to-roth-ira-rollovers/); they support B's bill-introduction details and dated survey description, so those were not treated as invented.
